newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Nov 21.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Chavalit Yongchaiyudh wins decree tussle but portfolio row heats up. Chavalit has ensured the early opening of the Lower House to consolidate his future as prime minister amid continuing conflict in his alliance over ecnomic portfolios. Banharn Silpa-archa, the outgoing prime minister, bowed to pressure from Chavalit's New Aspiration Party to seek royal approval to convene the Lower House quickly in order to activate the process to choose the Parliament president and the prime minister.

New Apiration has reached agreement with five smaller parties to form a government led by Chavalit. But the tug-of-war between New Aspiration and Chart Pattana, its second largest ally, for key portfolios prompted Chavalit to push the decree to secure his prospects. (BANGKOK POST)

- Banharn seen as worst-ever elected MP. Outgoing Prime Minister Banharn and his cabinet again turned a deaf ear to the public and on Tuesday approved the construction of the Kaeng Sua Ten dam. Not only is the act a breach of political ethics, but it also comes perilously close to being unconstitutional and illegal as the caretaker government has but a few days left in office. In addition, the controversial project was approved without any of required social and environmental studies being carried out. (THE NATION)

- Few foresee rate cuts this year. Most local bankers appear reluctant to cut interest rates, despite encouragement from the Bank of Thailand and assurances that the central bank would improve liquidity to make rate cuts easier to manage.

Few appear willing to follow the lead of Siam Commercial Bank, which cut its minimum retail rate (MRR) by a quarter percentage point recently. Piti Sithi-amnuay, executive vice president of Bangkok Bank, said lending rates were likely to remain the same or even increase between now and the end of the year, because this is the high season for consumption and exports. (BUSINESS POST) - Possible finance minister Amnuay Viravan seeks return of former SEC chief Ekamol Khiriwat. Scrambling to put together an economic "dream team" to bolster the incoming Chavalit administration, Amnuay yesterday produced an awesome list of local titans who would form an advisory powerhouse and help him tackle the economic mess.

Amnuay's list consisted of familiar names in Thai financial markets, including Narongchai Akrasanee, chairman of General Fiance & Securities; Ekamol Khiriwat, former Securities and Exchange Commission chief; Sirin Nimmanhaeminda, president of Krung Thai Bank; Viroj Nualkhair, chief execlutive of Phatra Thanakit; Pakhawat Kovitvathanaphong; Viroj Phutrakul, a former chairman of Lever Brothers (Thailand) Ltd; Olarn Chaipravat, president of Siam Commercial Bank; and Goanpoj Asvinvichitr, a senior executive of Union Bank of Bankok. (THE NATION)

- Bankers insist Amnuay must be given free rein. Bankers have thrown their support behind Amnuay, insisting he must be given a free hand to manage the country's economic policies. That free hand should include having the power to hand-pick the members of his economic team. But analysts said demands for these powers could open up cracks in the would-be coalition led by the New Aspiration party since the Chart Pattana Party, also wants to play a key role in the economic sphere. (BANGKOK POST)
